originality.rationale: The Weyl-ambiguity rank equivalence is acknowledged as prior. Seven actual semantic searches and six materially read primary/published result sources were compared by theorem implication. The closest published rational-positive odd-prime result covers a stronger arithmetic special case but not arbitrary even/noncyclic groups; the cyclic boxcar exact rank formula is restricted to interval indicators. No inspected result proves the all-abelian all-real-support sharp maximum with involution correction and constructive generic attainment. An equivalent theorem could be unindexed or implicit: this is self-review, not uniqueness certification.
residual_risks: A general generic-real-window result may be implicit in broader Heisenberg-covariant POVM theory and not indexed by the targeted terminology.
The Weyl matrix-rank equivalence is well established and is not claimed new; an alternate proof might make the remaining optimization short, without extinguishing the natural complete classification.
Published arithmetic-rigidity odd-prime and cyclic boxcar special cases are already covered and excluded from independent novelty claims.

value.rationale: For a natural fixed-support real-probe sensing question, determines exactly the greatest number of independently observable complex matrix directions for every finite abelian group, including all support masks and a simultaneous explicit attaining window. The answer depends structurally on the difference set and group two-torsion, distinguishing the order-eight group ranks 60,52,36. It precisely quantifies a real-probe obstruction, is not numerical census/one-off example, and does not incorrectly infer nonlinear phase-retrieval failure or robustness.
